newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up in cautious pre-GDP trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up in cautious pre-GDP trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks edged slightly up at the open on Monday in what traders said was cautious dealing ahead of key domestic and international economic data.
"It will be very quiet. Everyone is awaiting (domestic) GDP data, which look good, whereas opinions are mixed over the outcome of the FOMC meeting," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 2.29 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.06 percent, at 3,892.65. Trading volume of 2.5 million shares was inflated by cross trades, dealers said.

Mexico's Finance Ministry was expected to announce first quarter GDP figures in early trade. Finance Minister Ortiz told journalists last week he expected GDP to grow by 4.5-5.0 percent. This compares with 5.12 percent predicted in a previously conducted Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses.
The Federal Open Market Committee meeting will meet May 20 to review U.S. interest rates.
"I don't think (the FOMC) will have much impact here. As a preventative measure, it could hit us but would not knock us over," a desk trader said.
"We have stood up well to falls on the Dow Jones and will see mostly same-day in-and-out dealing," he added.
Telmex, the most heavily traded blue chip, was unchanged at 17.12 pesos.
On the broad market, of 18 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered sliders by six to five.
Steelmaker Grup IMSA headed the gainers' list, up 50 centavos to 22.20 pesos after one single cross trade.
Dealers said prominent sliders had mostly declined at thin volume and unrepresentative trade.
